contracts.docstring: Withdraw this project's native work and request legacy teardown where present; paused describes owner intent, not unproved physical closure.
Own one administrative domain and call trusted synchronous on_owner inside its scope before the first Git gate; retirement remains with the original broker.
Execute an original local-create/adopt/clone intent, registering only after original domain closure; exact completed retry starts nothing.
Recover original closure then observe only retained Git state in a fresh readonly domain; never repeat init/commit/clone or claim remote server termination.
Persist bounded original setup intents and directory ownership through the existing SQLite/project-metadata transaction.
Resolve and withdraw the current fence atomically for a bodyless whole-project Stop whose admission fuse already covers this original operation.
Immutable original administrative lease and actual broker, captured by the trusted executor before its first Git gate.
A browser observation can withdraw only this original owner; a later observation fence never inherits an older Stop.
Reuse the original broker's reserved Stop resources and retirement future; metadata is deliberately outside this physical path.
Own actual administrative worker handles without inventing native turns or replaying interrupted writes after restart.
Reuse the serving runtime's original host configuration, store, owner lock and kernel broker boundaries.
Bind actual executor ownership before G, conditionally withdrawing a late handoff only after its original requested identity matches.
Withdraw the already-captured original owner before cancelling its worker; late owners are held by the same local admission fuse.
Persist exact owner intent before scheduling one bounded worker; an original replay returns history and never restarts a stopped or uncertain effect.
Start only explicit readonly reconciliation of the retained operation; no implicit clone, initialization, commit or credentialed write is replayed.
Keep executor teardown in its owning task and retain failures as saved uncertainty; raw transport errors and secrets never enter the owner response.
Reject a mismatching captured original before any physical withdrawal; absent local ownership is not proof of remote or durable closure.
Hold one conditional original Stop through either individual or exact project persistence; it can withdraw only a matching real owner.
Withdraw an exact observed original owner before SQL, then persist intent and drain its actual worker without retargeting a new fence.
Withdraw only this application's actual administrative workers of the selected project before bodyless project Stop can wait on SQL.
Drain accepted source handoffs while the project or application fuse keeps late owners from receiving G.
Withdraw all currently recorded administrative work for the legacy bodyless project Stop, preserving uncertain original effects when no live handle exists.
Withdraw all owned source jobs before the runtime releases its exclusive store owner lock; cancellation is issued once and closure is drained.
Read-validated original project intent and immutable serialized scope; this host-only value is never accepted from an HTTP caller.
Return a detached original target set; mutating a consumer's copy cannot change the prepared authorization snapshot.
Recover a prior exact receipt without withdrawing any newer local owner.
Project real saved state without treating metadata as activity/closure or inventing a plan choice; no model, Git, remote setup or second coordinator.
Read exact native or administrative project Stop history before observing or withdrawing current work.
Validate the owner's complete observed scope in a readonly transaction before physical withdrawal; a history replay targets nothing new.
Atomically pause exactly observed graphs and withdraw exactly observed run authority before acknowledging intent; replay never retargets new work or claims closure.

One attempt's async composition and bounded launch/control resources.

One launch worker serializes accepted starts (at most eight pending). Peer
receipt work cannot occupy the separate worker reserved for whole-attempt
revocation. IO uses event-loop pipes, not blocking reader threads.
Withdraw G synchronously on the owning event loop and start the original physical retirement without awaiting source-local SQL.
Drain the single original retirement future; caller cancellation cannot transfer or cancel physical ownership.
Own native attempts and grant-bound tool closure before durable terminal states.
Compose one journal owner, native worker limits and deterministic authorized-plan dispatch; construction starts no work.
Withdraw exactly read-validated original local handles before the project Stop write; no cached later attempt can inherit this scope.
Withdraw current project owners before SQL and drain source handoffs under a temporary fuse; later explicit requests are never replayed by this Stop.
Withdraw every active native run in this project; returned states preserve unconfirmed physical closure rather than claiming all work stopped.
The existing runtime owns the kernel domain; SQL fences and exact owner targets precede local withdrawal, while a replay returns only the original intent receipt.
Serve real smart HTTP Git over verified local TLS plus a small controlled Forgejo REST contract; all effect actors are fixture-owned.
Bounded fixture protocol handler; authentication values are never logged or saved as artifacts.
Authenticate by protocol, then execute only this temporary repository or its explicit REST model.
Observe the actual original broker's returned kernel DomainClosure; journal sealing is checked after persistence drains, without polling its mutation lock.
A real TLS clone remains blocked at its server while its exact local kernel domain closes despite an unrelated source-store writer.
The exact prior project Stop returns its old receipt while SQLite is busy and another actual source clone remains alive, never borrowing the new owner.

scope: New/changed Python definitions and modules in this delivery. Relevant new frontend modules and exported helpers also carry English JSDoc; no claim that all historic project definitions are documented.
